The pinned Node 24.22.3 Alpine 3.24 and Go 1.27.4 Alpine 3.24 FROM digests contain zlib 1.3.2-r1; fixed in 1.4-r0. Production and development Dockerfiles install and assert zlib 1.4-r0 before project build/runtime commands. The hosted production image is scratch and does not ship the builder package. Nox inventories FROM metadata and cannot verify the post-RUN package state, so this baseline records that scanner limitation and is not evidence the upstream images are fixed. Tracked in https://github.com/felixgeelhaar/ghostline/issues/58; remove when Nox can verify built image contents or the pinned FROM digests contain fixed zlib.

The pinned Go 1.27.4 Alpine 3.24 FROM digest contains zlib 1.3.2-r1; fixed in 1.4-r0. The development Dockerfile installs and asserts zlib 1.4-r0 before running Ghostline. Nox inventories FROM metadata and cannot verify post-RUN package state. Temporary scanner limitation tracked in https://github.com/felixgeelhaar/ghostline/issues/58; remove when Nox can verify built image contents or the pinned FROM digest contains fixed zlib.

Second occurrence of the same zlib finding at the Go builder FROM in Dockerfile. This base digest contains zlib 1.3.2-r1; the build upgrades and asserts 1.4-r0 before compiling Ghostline. The hosted image is scratch and does not ship the builder package. Nox currently emits one fingerprint for both FROM lines, so a second documented baseline entry is required to represent both occurrences. This is not evidence the pinned upstream image is fixed. Tracked in https://github.com/felixgeelhaar/ghostline/issues/58; remove when Nox can verify built image contents or the pinned FROM digest contains fixed zlib.

Temporary maintainer-approved release exception through 2026-11-20, tracked in https://github.com/felixgeelhaar/ghostline/issues/45. Nox identifies OpenSSL 3.5.9 in the pinned Node builder; this root Dockerfile uses Node only to build static assets, and the hosted runtime is scratch. Reachability is undetermined, so this is accepted interim risk, not a claim the advisories are fixed. Remove as soon as a supported Node release ships OpenSSL 3.5.10 or later.
